title: ablation-dist-preflight has no CI wiring for its self-test (which just grew by 28 cases), and its header names a document that never mentions it

⚠️ Both items are **pre-existing** and were ⛔ NOT introduced by PR #19640. They are carded rather than folded into it because ① is a maintainer-floor item (adding a required gate) and ② lands on a governed Tier S surface — neither is a dev's to take inside that PR's fence.

## ① `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` has NO CI wiring at all, and its self-test just grew

The script's `--self-test` is not run anywhere. Measured on `origin/main`: **zero** hits for the script name in `package.json`, `.github/**` and `turbo.json`. Positive control on the same command and scope fired — `check:pm-expected-skips` resolves at `package.json:99` — so the instrument discriminates and the zero is a reading.

**Why it matters now rather than in general.** PR #19640 adds **28** self-test cases (to 64, over 5 batteries) and raises `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` from 3 to 5. ⇒ the amount of behaviour resting on an unrun self-test just grew substantially. At the reviewed head the **only** evidence those 64 cases pass is a reviewer's hand run in a throwaway worktree. And PR #19640 carries `skip-changeset`, which is the second half of the shape below.

**The repo has a named precedent for exactly this inversion.** `.github/workflows/lint.yml` documents PR #6876 (#5620) adding five assertions to a checker that "never executed once on its own CI" because it carried `skip-changeset`. The prescribed remedy there was a **deliberately unconditional self-test step** in `lint.yml`.

⚠️ The split matters and the card does not blur it: the script's **run** half legitimately cannot be a gate — it judges a deliberately mutated tree, which CI never has. The **`--self-test`** half has no such obstacle and is what every sibling `check:X` entry in this repo wires.

⛔ This is a **maintainer-floor** item by the standing rule (「新增必需门禁/hook/棘轮」), so it is filed rather than fixed. ⛔ No remedy is prescribed here beyond naming the precedent; whether to wire it, and how unconditionally, is the maintainer's call.

Dedupe words: `ablation-dist-preflight` · `self-test not in CI` · `#6876` · `#5620` · `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR`

## ② The script's header names a document that does not mention it

`scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`'s header names `.claude/skills/dogfood-verification/SKILL.md` as one of "three documents that state this script's invocation". That file mentions the script **0 times** — measured, 148 lines.

Identical at base, so ⛔ not a regression from PR #19640. It is worth a row anyway because that PR rewrote the surrounding header **specifically to make the instrument's claims exact**, and this one is checkable and false.

⚠️ The fix lands in `.claude/**`, a **governed Tier S** surface (`GOVERNED_SURFACES`, id `claude-tree`, "the agent instruction tree") — or in the script's header, depending which side a taker judges wrong. ⛔ Either way it cannot ride a code PR's fence without the governed-surface path.

⚠️ The same round noted a sibling item and deliberately did not file it: the two documents that **do** state the invocation (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md:255`, `packages/qa/dogfood/README.md:54`) show only the default present-mode form, while PR #19640 makes the pristine-build present-mode reading the presence evidence a DELETE ablation owes. The round recorded the successor as **NONE** — both files are outside that PR's fence and no queued PR touches them. Named here so it is not lost, ⛔ not asserted as a defect.
